page_title: Model Salt: one prompt, ten different answers

sources.entry: Model Salt - Open source MCP server with one tool: before a creative task the model gets a few choices drawn from atmospheric and quantum noise, so one prompt gives different answers that still do what was asked. #free #opensource #mcp

summary.name: Model Salt
summary.one_liner: Model Salt is an open source MCP server with one tool, model_salt, that feeds randomness from outside the model into open creative tasks so each run gives a different answer that still fits the request.
use_cases: Getting varied name suggestions from an AI assistant
Producing different creative takes on the same prompt
Generating varied SVG or image concepts from one prompt
Avoiding the same answer repeated across runs
Adding controlled randomness to coding agent open choices
summary.what_it_does: Model Salt is a single MCP tool, model_salt. Before an open-ended task, the model calls it once, and it returns choices settled by randomness drawn from outside the model, which the model then uses to do the work. A randomness setting from 0 to 2 controls the spread: 0 keeps the usual answer, 1 is the default, and 2 makes every answer equally likely. The page also describes a no-install option: a single message pasted into ChatGPT or Gemini that draws fresh random numbers, shows five choices with their odds, and asks before generating anything. Setup is via npx -y @modelsalt/model-salt for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Kimi, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Zed and other stdio MCP clients.
notable: Draws choice randomness from atmospheric and quantum noise rather than the model's own sampling
Adjustable randomness dial from 0 to 2 with default 1
Works as a one-line npx install across many MCP clients, requires Node 18 or later and no keys
Open source; a no-install paste-in message version works in ChatGPT or Gemini
caveats: Requires Node 18 or later to run the npx MCP server
Setting 2 makes every answer equally likely, which may drift from what was asked
The no-install version is a pasted message that must be re-pressed for new numbers; reusing a message gives the same picks
